{% autoescape off %}# Sealbill API

Invoicing service for organizations. JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: {{ site_url }}/api/v1
OpenAPI 3.1 schema: {{ site_url }}/api/v1/schema   Human docs: {{ site_url }}/api/v1/docs

## Authentication
Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request. A token belongs to one organization and
sees only that organization's contacts and invoices (invoices it requested, or that it issues).
Tokens are created by an operator: `manage.py create_api_token --org <slug> --name <n> --scopes read,invoices:write`.
Wrong, missing or revoked token: 401. Missing scope: 403. Over 120 requests a minute per token: 429.
While the service is sealed (after a restart, until an operator unlocks it) every call answers
503 {"error": "vault_sealed"}; retry later.

## Scopes
- read: every GET.
- invoices:write: create/update contacts and their encryption keys, create/send/void invoices, reissue links, create/update/deactivate/rotate payment links.
- payments:confirm: confirm/reject/reverse/assign payments, acknowledge refunds, dismiss declarations. THIS MOVES MONEY STATE.
  It does not record manual payments: only a person records a manual payment, on the staff pages.
- admin: implies all of the above, and manages webhooks (/api/v1/webhooks).

## Errors
Every error is {"error": "<code>", "detail": ...}. 400 validation_error / invalid_request (fix the request),
409 invoice_error (the object is in the wrong state, e.g. sending twice, voiding a paid invoice), 409 needs_person (only a
person on the staff pages may do this; no token can). Never retry a 409 blindly.

## Lists
GET list endpoints (contacts, invoices, payments, declarations, payment-links) are paginated: {"count": N, "next": url|null,
"previous": url|null, "results": [...]}. Use ?limit= (default 50, max 200) and ?offset=. A row whose stored value
cannot be decrypted appears as {"id": N, "error": "undecryptable"} instead of failing the page.
Error 503 vault_sealed means the service is locked; 500 undecryptable means one stored value is unreadable (staff are alerted).

## Money
All amounts are integers in minor units (cents). Quantities are decimal strings with at most 2 places. Rates are basis points (2000 = 20%).

## Endpoints
GET  /api/v1/me                  (read) {"organization", "token", "scopes": [...]}: who this token is
GET  /api/v1/contacts[?email=<exact address, case-insensitive>: zero or one contact], GET /api/v1/contacts/{id}
                                 Every contact carries "has_paid_invoice" (boolean): true when an invoice that staff or the
                                 API issued to it (or to the copy the US-resident organization keeps of it) is paid or
                                 overpaid, never a payment-link order, whatever it cost. Offer only such contacts as
                                 evidence of a client.
GET  /api/v1/contacts?name=<text>   (read) 2-100 characters; every word must be a whole word of the legal or display name
                                 (case and accents folded; a hyphen separates words, so "jean" and "luc" both match "Jean-Luc"). At most 20 results,
                                 30 searches per minute per token (429 throttled), your token's own organization only, never
                                 the copies kept for another organization. Not combinable with email (400)
POST /api/v1/contacts            {"email", "legal_name", ...}  201 new, 200 existing e-mail
PATCH /api/v1/contacts/{id}      the fields given; they reach the copy the US-resident organization keeps of this contact
                                 for your organization too (never its own client, never another organization's copy)
GET  /api/v1/contacts/{id}/keys  (read) the contact's encryption keys: {"id", "kind": "pgp|smime", "fingerprint",
                                 "state": "pending|active|replaced|revoked|failed", "expires_at", "source"}; never the key itself
POST /api/v1/contacts/{id}/keys  {"key": "<ASCII-armored PGP public key or PEM certificate>"}  (invoices:write)
                                 active at once, replaces the previous key; e-mail to the contact is then encrypted to it.
                                 400 key_rejected with the reason in "detail" (expired, email_mismatch, secret_key, ...);
                                 503 key_check_unavailable: nothing was stored, retry shortly
POST /api/v1/keys/{id}/revoke    (invoices:write) the key is never used again
GET  /api/v1/invoices?external_reference=&status=&limit=&offset=
GET  /api/v1/invoices/{id}       totals, lines, status, "amount_paid_minor" and "balance_due_minor" (total less confirmed
                                 payments, floored at 0; the balance means nothing when status is "void"; an excess is "amount_paid_minor" less
                                 "totals.total"). An ordinary crypto overpayment shows as
                                 "paid" with "refund_due_base_units" set on the payment, not as "overpaid"; never contains the client links
POST /api/v1/invoices            create a DRAFT (no money moves, nothing is sent). Optional "return_url": an https address on a
                                 host in the organization setting "return_url_hosts" (else 400 return_url_not_allowed); the client's
                                 page then shows a Back link to it. The page never redirects there by itself.
                                 Optional "method_kinds": ["bank", "fiat_link", "rail"], resolved against the issuing
                                 organization (the US rule applied) into the offered methods; send it OR "offered_methods", not both
                                 (400 methods_conflict); nothing resolving is 409 no_methods
POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/send  {"email_client": true, "client_letters": true}  draft -> sent; numbers it; returns view_url and
                                 pay_url ONCE. "email_client": false only skips the invoice letter. "client_letters": false means
                                 NO letter about this invoice ever goes to the client from this system (invoice, receipt, partial
                                 receipt, new links), for a caller that writes to the client itself. It is per invoice, fixed at send, not a
                                 mute on the contact; encryption-key e-mails are unaffected; staff alerts still go out.
                                 Combining "client_letters": false with "email_client": true is 400.
                                 With "client_letters": true (the default) the system also sends ONE reminder letter about an unpaid
                                 invoice (sent, overdue or partially paid) INVOICE_REMINDER_DAYS (30) days after sending, to a
                                 client of record with an e-mail address. The reminder REPLACES both links, so links you gave the client
                                 by other means stop working, and it emits invoice.links_reissued. Send with "client_letters": false
                                 to be left out
POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/reissue-links   replaces both links (old ones stop working, and e-mails not yet sent with
                                 them are cancelled); returns them ONCE
POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/void  {"reason": "..."}  refused when confirmed money exists, and while a payment is detected
                                 (409 "invoice_error" either way)
GET  /api/v1/invoices/{id}/pdf   application/pdf. Once sent, the PDF and the client's pages keep the seller, buyer and
                                 payment details the invoice was sent with; later edits of those records do not change it
POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/payments  {"amount_minor", "rail": "bank|fiat_link|manual", "note"}  refused for every token: 409
                                 needs_person, nothing is written (only a person records a manual payment, on the staff pages)
GET  /api/v1/payment-methods?currency=EUR&contact_email=client@example.com   (read) which organization would issue
                                 the invoice (US rule applied to the contact, if known) and the methods it would offer:
                                 {"currency", "issuer_org", "issued_by_rule", "methods": [{"id": "bank:3", "kind", "label", "currencies"}]}
GET  /api/v1/payments[?invoice=<id>]   one invoice's payments
GET  /api/v1/payment-links       (read) your organization's payment links, paged; never their URLs
GET  /api/v1/payment-links/{id}  (read) one link with its "url": the public page anyone can pay through. The URL is a
                                 capability, handed out here, on create and on rotate only: pass it on to whoever should have it
POST /api/v1/payment-links       (invoices:write) {"title", "currency", "price_minor" | "customer_chooses": true with optional
                                 "min_minor"/"max_minor", "description", "tax_rate_bps", "max_quantity" (0: any, up to 200),
                                 "name_field"/"billing_field"/"shipping_field"/"phone_field" off|optional|required, "custom_fields":
                                 [{"label", "required"}] (up to 5), "kind": invoice|payment_request, "methods": default|custom with
                                 "method_types", "fulfillment", "notify_staff", "active", "valid_until", "max_uses"}.
                                 201 with the link and its "url"; 400 with the reason when a rule is broken
PATCH /api/v1/payment-links/{id} (invoices:write) the fields given. {"active": false} deactivates: the page then says the link is
                                 no longer available; orders already made are untouched. The URL does not change
POST /api/v1/payment-links/{id}/rotate   (invoices:write) a new URL; the old one stops working at once; returns the link with it
                                 Another organization's link is 404. Every change is recorded in the audit log, as made through the API.
                                 Invoices made from a link carry "payment_link_id" and "coupon_code" (null otherwise).
GET  /api/v1/exports/invoices.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD   (read) CSV for the books: the invoices your
                                 organization requested, including those the US-resident organization issued on its behalf
                                 (the US tax resident rule), and those it issued itself; at most 400 days (else 400 bad_range)
GET  /api/v1/exports/payments.csv?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD   (read) the payments on those invoices (an admin token
                                 also gets those no invoice holds yet that your organization may be credited with), with
                                 network, tx hash and quote rate
POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/confirm   {"note"}   detected/needs_review -> confirmed (may mark the invoice paid);
                                 409 needs_person when the payment reads "needs_staff_confirmation": true
POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/reject    {"note"}
POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/reverse   {"reason"} confirmed -> reversed (reason required)
GET  /api/v1/invoices/{id}/quotes, GET /api/v1/quotes/{id}   (read) crypto quotes of an invoice
POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/quotes    {"method": "rail:3", "network": "arbitrum", "asset": "USDC", "refresh": false}  (invoices:write)
POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/assign    {"invoice_id", "amount_minor", "note"}  (payments:confirm, Idempotency-Key REQUIRED)
POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/acknowledge-refund   {"note"}  (payments:confirm)
GET  /api/v1/declarations            clients' "I have paid" claims. A declaration is a claim, not money.
POST /api/v1/declarations/{id}/dismiss {"reason"}

## Crypto payments and quotes
An invoice offers crypto through "rail:<id>" methods (GET /api/v1/payment-methods lists each rail with its "options":
[{"network", "asset"}] pairs). A client does not pay "the invoice amount" in crypto: they pay a QUOTE. POST
/api/v1/invoices/{id}/quotes {"method", "network", "asset"} fixes the exchange rate and returns the exact amount to send:
"amount_base_units" (integer, the asset's smallest unit) and "amount" (the same in whole units), "address", "payment_uri",
or for BTCPay/Lightning a "checkout_url" / "bolt11". A quote lives about 30 minutes ("expires_at"). "money_may_be_coming" (read-only boolean) is true for a BTCPay/Lightning quote whose money the
gateway has seen but not settled, or that nobody has read successfully since it expired; and for a chain quote while it still
holds its amount (until it is released, about a day after it closes), while the watcher of its account and network is failing
or has not read since it expired, or while skipped blocks of its address wait for a person: never void the invoice while any quote says so.
"money_may_be_coming_reason" says which, or is "" when the flag is false: "quote_held" (a chain quote still holds its amount;
it ends by itself about a day after the quote closes), "watcher_failing", "watcher_behind" (the chain scan has not read since
the quote expired), "blocks_not_scanned" (skipped blocks wait for a person) or "gateway" (a BTCPay/Lightning quote). The watcher
reasons last as long as the outage. On a shared address the
amount is UNIQUE per quote (it is how the payment is matched): send exactly that amount, never a rounded one. An open quote
for the same method, network and asset is returned again (200) until it nears expiry; "refresh": true cancels it and issues a
new one. Do not create quotes speculatively: each holds its amount for about a day, and one invoice holds at most 20 that
are not yet released (a further one is refused with too_many_quotes until one is released).
Quote errors are 409 {"error": <code>} with not_payable, method_not_offered, asset_not_enabled, nothing_due, rates_diverge,
no_free_amount, too_many_quotes or rail_unavailable; "rates_unavailable" is 503 (retry in a minute). Nothing was created in either case.
A crypto payment in GET /api/v1/payments has rail, network, asset, amount_base_units, tx_hash, log_index, "final",
"quote", and: "state": "needs_review" with a "review_reason" when no invoice matched it or something looks wrong; a person
or an agent holding payments:confirm moves it on. A payment waiting for a person ("needs_staff_confirmation": true) moves on
only by a person, on the staff pages: confirm and assign by any token, admin included, answer 409 "needs_person" and change
nothing. Calls that MOVE MONEY STATE (never repeat blindly):
- POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/assign   attach a needs_review payment to one invoice of your organization and credit
  "amount_minor" (invoice currency). A chain transfer needs "final": true (a gateway payment in review may be assigned while it reads false). Needs a note and an Idempotency-Key. Refused unless your organization
  owns the account the money reached (accepted even if that account is now inactive) or holds another active account with
  that address on that network.
- POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/acknowledge-refund   record that "refund_due_base_units" (paid beyond the quote) was refunded
  or will not be. Once only.
- POST /api/v1/payments/{id}/confirm, /reject, /reverse   as above; confirm refuses a chain transfer that is not yet deep
  enough in the chain. A payment that is confirmed reads "final": true whatever its rail (one a person confirmed after it waited
  for them, a manual payment, one assigned from review); "final": false means not confirmed yet: a chain transfer below finality, or a gateway payment not settled or waiting for a person.
A payment with no invoice yet is visible to admin tokens only.

## Webhooks (admin scope)
Signed notifications of what happens to your organization's invoices and payments. Manage them with an admin token:
GET  /api/v1/webhooks             your endpoints; never the secret, and a URL's query string shows as "?..."
POST /api/v1/webhooks             {"url": "https://...", "events": ["invoice.paid", "payment.confirmed"], "description": "..."}
                                  201 with "secret" ONCE: store it, it is never shown again. "events" defaults to ["*"] (all).
                                  400 webhook_refused, "detail": scheme | private_address | unresolvable | bad_url | port (only 443) | endpoint_limit. https only, and
                                  the host must resolve to public addresses only (no loopback, private, link-local, multicast).
GET  /api/v1/webhooks/{id}, DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{id}   (delete: the endpoint, its secret and its delivery log go)
GET  /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries   the delivery log: "state" queued|sent|failed|cancelled, "attempts", "last_status_code",
                                  "last_error_kind" (http_503, redirect, timeout, tls, connection, refused:<code>), timestamps
POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/ping   queues a "ping" event for that endpoint alone (202); the worker sends it within about 15 s

Events: invoice.created, invoice.sent, invoice.voided, invoice.declared (a client says they paid: a claim, not money),
invoice.partially_paid, invoice.paid, invoice.overpaid (the invoice reached that status),
invoice.links_reissued (staff made new links in the staff pages, or the 30-day reminder did, so the pay and view URLs you stored are dead; "data" has
invoice_id and status. The API's reissue-links call does not emit it: its caller has the new links), payment.detected (seen, not final
yet), payment.confirmed, payment.needs_review (a person must decide), payment.rejected, payment.reversed, staff.alert
("data.kind": watcher = a payment watcher cannot see its chain, vault_unlock_failures = repeated failed vault unlock attempts,
payment_invalid_after_confirmation = the gateway now calls a payment it had settled invalid (a person must look), outbox_failed = e-mail could not be delivered, key_failed = a
client's encryption key stopped working, key_cancel = the holder of a client's previous key cancelled a newly uploaded one,
or was refused: data.reason cancelled | replaced_key_withdrawn | cannot_restore), ping. An invoice you requested that another organization issued (the US tax resident
rule) is reported to both organizations.

Each delivery is one POST, Content-Type: application/json, with the body
{"created_at": "2026-11-03T10:00:00.000Z", "data": {"invoice_id": 42, "status": "paid"}, "id": "<event uuid>", "org": "<slug>", "type": "invoice.paid"}
("org" is null for a staff.alert about the service itself). "data" is thin: ids, statuses and kinds only, never names,
e-mails, amounts or addresses. Every key it may carry:
  invoice_id, payment_id, declaration_id, endpoint_id (ping), key_id (staff.alert key_failed, key_cancel): ids
  status (the invoice's, or the payment's on payment.*), invoice_status (payment.reversed), kind (invoice.created: invoice |
  payment_request; staff.alert: watcher | vault_unlock_failures | payment_invalid_after_confirmation | outbox_failed | key_failed | key_cancel), rail (payment.*), reason (a review or
  refusal code)
  count, watchers (watcher names), networks (staff.alert: how many, and which)
Read the invoice or payment through the API for the rest; that is also its current state.
Headers: X-Pay-Event (the type), X-Pay-Event-Id (the event id, the same on every retry), X-Pay-Signature: sha256=<hex>.

Verify every delivery before trusting it: HMAC-SHA256 with your secret over the RAW request body, exactly the bytes received
(never parse and re-serialize first), compared in constant time:
    import hashlib, hmac
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, request.headers.get("X-Pay-Signature", "")):
        return 401  # not from us, or altered on the way
(Node: compare equal-length Buffers with crypto.timingSafeEqual; never with == or ===.)
Answer 2xx within 10 seconds and do the work afterwards. Anything else, a redirect included (redirects are never followed), is
retried after 2, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 240 and 480 minutes (about 16 hours); then the delivery is failed and staff are told.
Delivery is at least once and not necessarily in order: deduplicate on X-Pay-Event-Id and re-read the object for its state.
"created_at" is inside the signed body, so you may refuse an event older than you are willing to accept.
An event that happens while the service is sealed is recorded and delivered once an operator unlocks it.

## Idempotency
POST /api/v1/invoices accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header and/or an `external_reference` body field, both scoped
to your organization. Repeating the call returns the same invoice with 200 instead of 201, so it is safe to retry.
Always send one of them. The request is fingerprinted (the inline contact with all its fields, currency, kind,
lines, due_days, offered_methods, return_url, method_kinds, title, notes): reusing a key or reference with a DIFFERENT body is 409 "idempotency_mismatch",
never a silent return of the old invoice. Keys are at most 200 characters. (Invoices created before November 2026 carry
no fingerprint: a repeat returns them whatever the body.)
POST /api/v1/invoices/{id}/payments records nothing for a token (409 needs_person); a key a person already used there
returns that payment with 200, a different body 409 idempotency_mismatch. Send and void calls are NOT idempotent: a second
send is a 409, so check GET /api/v1/invoices/{id} before repeating after a timeout.

## US tax residents
If the contact has "us_tax_resident": "yes", the invoice is issued by the US-resident organization whatever you asked for.
The response then has "issued_by_rule": true and "issuer_org" differs from "requested_by_org".
A draft made before the contact became a US tax resident is refused at send (409 invoice_error, "contact is a US
tax resident: delete this draft and create it again"): void it and create the invoice again; nothing is re-issued silently.

## Contacts made by payment links
A payment-link checkout whose e-mail matches no contact makes a contact of its own from what the visitor typed (a link
buyer). It is not a client of record, and paying does not change that: anyone can pay a link under any name. No list,
e-mail or name lookup returns it, GET/PATCH by its id is 404, "contact_id" naming it is 400, and an inline "contact" with
its e-mail makes a new contact from your fields, so a visitor's data never reaches your invoice. Only a person on the staff
pages makes a link buyer a client of record. A checkout whose e-mail matches a contact books the order to it and changes
nothing on it.

## Contacts inside an invoice request
"contact": {"email": ...} finds the contact by e-mail or creates it. For an EXISTING contact the other fields are ignored,
except "us_tax_resident": "yes" is applied (upgrade; the issuer rule then switches the issuer). Sending a different value
for a contact stored as "yes" is 409 "contact_conflict": PATCH /api/v1/contacts/{id} first.
"offered_methods" items are "bank:<id>", "fiat:<id>" or "rail:<id>" (a crypto rail) of an active account of the issuing organization,
else 400 "invalid_offered_method"; a bank account must be in the invoice currency, a crypto rail takes any currency. Omit
"offered_methods" to offer the issuer's defaults: its active bank accounts in the invoice currency, its active fiat links that
accept it and its active crypto rails (GET /api/v1/payment-methods shows them beforehand). An invoice that
offers nothing ("offered_methods": [] or no matching account) is refused at send: 409 invoice_error "no payment method offered".
Limits: quantity at most 10 integer and 2 decimal digits; amounts, and the invoice total, at most 10^12 minor units
(a larger total is 400 invoice_error); due_days 0..3650; at most 200 lines; title at most 2000, notes 5000, a line's name
500 and its description 2000 characters; issue_date from 2000-01-01 to 365 days from today (else 400 validation_error). Unknown /api/v1 paths answer 404 {"error": "not_found"}.

## Example
curl -X POST {{ site_url }}/api/v1/invoices \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: order-1042" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"contact": {"email": "client@example.com", "legal_name": "Client Ltd"}, "currency": "EUR",
       "due_days": 14, "lines": [{"name": "Consulting", "quantity": "1", "unit_price_minor": 10000, "tax_rate_bps": 2000}]}'
curl -X POST {{ site_url }}/api/v1/invoices/ID/send -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email_client": true}'
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" {{ site_url }}/api/v1/invoices?external_reference=order-1042
